title: Head bounds during a captured loop prefix
statement: Let $B,t$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{body}$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $a$ be a state of $\mathrm{body}$, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Take a Boolean value $\mathrm{startup}$, a configuration $c$ of $\mathrm{body}$ on $x$, a Boolean value $\mathrm{release}$, a Boolean word $\mathrm{word}$, and a configuration $\mathrm{fuel}$ of $F$ on $x$. Assume that $c$ is not halted, all its work-tape heads start at position zero, the computation from $c$ is not halted at any time $u<t$, and for every $u<t$ either $u=0$ and $\mathrm{release}$ is true or the state at time $u$ is not $a$. Assume also that the computation from $c$ uses at most $B$ work-tape cells through every time $u\le t$, all work-tape heads of $\mathrm{fuel}$ lie in $[-B,B]$, and the output at time $t$ has length at most $B$. Then throughout every time $u\le t$, every work-tape head in the loop host computation started from the captured call with startup value $\mathrm{startup}$, release value $\mathrm{release}$, no flag, word $\mathrm{word}$, and fuel configuration $\mathrm{fuel}$ lies in $[-B,B]$.
